original_question: Suppose phi: X -> Y is an almost holomorphic map between smooth projective varieties, pi: Gamma -> X resolves its indeterminacy, D is an effective divisor on Gamma such that (Gamma, D) is klt, and -pi_*(K_{Gamma/Y} + D) is nef. Under these relative anti-canonical assumptions, can one obtain a structure theorem, and in particular can one choose a holomorphic morphism X -> Y' that is birationally equivalent to the original map phi: X -> Y?
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual open problem. It correctly captures the relative anti-canonical setup: an almost holomorphic map ϕ:X⇢Y between smooth projective varieties, a resolution π:Γ→X of the indeterminacy of ϕ, an effective divisor D on Γ with (Γ,D) klt, and the nefness assumption on -π_*(K_{Γ/Y}+D). It also correctly identifies the main question asked in the paper: whether one can obtain a structure theorem under these hypotheses and, in particular, replace the rational map by a holomorphic morphism to a birational model of the target.
missing_details: The paper is working over the complex numbers; the varieties are complex smooth projective varieties.
To make the setup self-contained, one should introduce the induced morphism φ:Γ→Y after resolving the indeterminacy of ϕ, and define K_{Γ/Y}:=K_Γ-φ^*K_Y.
The boundary D should be stated as an effective Q-divisor (or at least as a divisor defining a klt pair), and -π_*(K_{Γ/Y}+D) is a nef Q-divisor on X.

The paper emphasizes that ϕ is not assumed to be an RC fibration; this is essential, because the analogous holomorphic-model conclusion is already explained as known when the general fibers are rationally connected.
The target Y' should be specified as a smooth projective birational model of Y.
The phrase 'birationally equivalent' should be unpacked: one wants a morphism f:X→Y' and a birational map μ:Y'⇢Y such that ϕ=μ∘f as rational maps.

For full paper-faithfulness, the question should be phrased as asking for a structure theorem under the relative anti-canonical hypothesis, with the existence of a holomorphic model singled out as the concrete test case.
refined_question: Let X and Y be smooth projective varieties over C, let ϕ:X⇢Y be an almost holomorphic rational map (i.e. its general fibers are compact), and let π:Γ→X be a resolution of the indeterminacy of ϕ, with induced morphism φ:Γ→Y. Assume that there exists an effective Q-divisor D on Γ such that (Γ,D) is klt and the Q-divisor -π_*(K_{Γ/Y}+D) on X is nef, where K_{Γ/Y}=K_Γ-φ^*K_Y. Without assuming that ϕ is an RC fibration, does this relative anti-canonical hypothesis imply a structure theorem analogous to the one known when the general fibers are rationally connected? In particular, after replacing Y by a smooth projective birational model Y', does there exist a holomorphic morphism f:X→Y' and a birational map μ:Y'⇢Y such that ϕ=μ∘f as rational maps?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 5.2 almost verbatim. In Section 5, after stating Theorem 5.1 for smooth klt pairs with nef anti-canonical divisor, the paper explains that many of the arguments extend to a relative setting: one starts with an almost holomorphic map ϕ:X⇢Y, resolves it by π:Γ→X with induced morphism φ:Γ→Y, and assumes the existence of an effective divisor D such that (Γ,D) is klt and -π_*(K_{Γ/Y}+D) is nef. The paper then notes that, if the general fibers of ϕ are rationally connected, the direct-image flatness results lead to a splitting of TX and allow one to replace the rational map by a holomorphic morphism to another smooth birational model of Y; the unresolved point is whether this remains true when ϕ is not an RC fibration. That unresolved question is exactly Problem 5.2.
